sub_strands.title: Drawing
learning_outcomes: a) analyze the elements and principles of 2 dimensional art in drawing,
b) draw objects in one-point perspective,
c) draw objects in two - point perspective
d) apply the stages of drawing in executing a still life composition,
e) make a portfolio folder for storage and presentation of artworks,
f) value drawing as a technique in picture making.
learning_experiences: use digital devices to source and study artworks in the actual and virtual environment focusing on; - Elements:line; (contour/lines),shape,(overlapping), texture (tactile /simulated), value (tinting/shading), colour (hue,value, intensity) - Principles-balance, dominance,proportion, rhythm and movement, harmony/unity of 2D Art art in drawing,
explore objects in actual and safe virtual sources to visualize occurrence of linear perspective with focus on one -point perspective,
draw angular objects in one- point perspective with emphasis on: convergence lines,vanishing point and one view point,
explore objects in actual and safe virtual sources to visualize occurrence of linear perspective with focus on two-point perspective,
draw angular objects and spaces in two-point perspective with emphasis on:convergence lines, two vanishing points and view points,
collectively gather a variety of objects, set up a still life observing overlaps and sizes of objects and draw it with focus on :sketching, shading (smudge), adding details and refining,
use recyclable materials to make a one fold portfolio folder to store 2 dimensional artworks,
present the drawings in the portfolio for critique and feedback.
key_inquiry_questions: How can perspective create an illusion of depth in a drawing?

sub_strands.title: Painting
learning_outcomes: a) describe wash techniques of painting,
b) paint sceneries from observation using the wash technique,
c) describe brush-spraying techniques of painting
d) create a pictorial composition using brush-spray painting technique,
learning_experiences: search virtual and/or actual sources to study samples of paintings done using the wash techniques, with emphasis on:wash technique (flat and graded}
experiment with flat washes and graded washes on paper using water colours,
make a viewfinder using recycled paper
explore the environment and use the viewfinder to select sceneries for painting, with focus on foreground, middleground, background and dominance.
key_inquiry_questions: Why is the wash technique most appropriate for painting sceneries?
How do flat and graded washes compare in terms of their application, challenges and techniques?

sub_strands.title: Graphic Design
learning_outcomes: a) analyse the concept of calligraphy for farmiliarity,
b) illustrate short text for a seasonal card using calligraphy,
c) design a trade mark using computer aided design,
d) design a poster using line and wash illustrations
e) appraise own and others' calligraphy, trademarks and posters.
learning_experiences: watch videos on calligraphy and engagingly discuss; making the pen (cutting of the tip), angle of writing, and stylisation of ascenders, body ,descenders,
use recyclable materials to improvise 2 calligraphy pens (flat and slanted tip),
practise writing letters,numeral among others,
use guidelines to write text maintaining the correct angle of the pen to write a seasonal card in lower case,
effectively research on elements of graphic design (illustrations, layout, colour, and lettering),
use computer aided design to create a 2 colour trademark,
observe actual or virtual samples of educational, social and advertisement posters,
create an advertisement poster in freehand with emphasis on;line and wash illustrations, layout, colour and dominance
display and critique others’ works while reflecting on own illustrations.
key_inquiry_questions: Why are graphic illustrations incorporated in a work of Art?
Why should one use a slanted tip when improvising a calligraphy pen?

sub_strands.title: Fabric Decoration:Tie and Dye
learning_outcomes: a) analyse the concept of tie and dyed in fabric decoration,
b) tie and dye fabric to create diamond effect,
c) tie and dye fabric to create spiral effects,
d) appraise own and others' decorated fabrics .
learning_experiences: explore actual and virtual sources to research tie and dye focusing on; concept, techniques (diamond and spiral methods) and materials and tools,
actively collaborate in sourcing and preparing the cotton fabrics enough for the methods,
tie the fabric according to the technique (diamond and spiral methods),
prepare the two dye baths according to manufacturer instructions while observing safety,
dye the fabric in two colours for each method,
rinse, dry and iron the fabric to make a scarf/ table clothe while observing safety precautions,
collaboratively display and have peer assessment of t
key_inquiry_questions: What is the cultural significance of tye and dye?
How do the different binding techniques affect the resultant patterns?

sub_strands.title: Pottery and Ceramics
learning_outcomes: a) analyse properties of clay in pottery,
b) prepare clay for pottery,
c) model a hand-built vase using the pellet technique,
d) fire the pellet vases in an updraught kiln,
e) appraise the hand-built pellet vases for feedback.
learning_experiences: research virtual and/actual sources on pottery focusing on; practise in Kenya, properties (plasticity, porosity, vitrification) and preparation of clay.
source clay,drying, crushing, slaking,sieving,drying, kneading and wedging; and store for use,
watch a video on pellet technique to analyse uniformity and joining of pellets,
model a clay vase using the pellet technique with emphasis on uniformity of pellets joinery of clay pellets considering elements and principles of 3D Art,
collaboratively use recyclable materials to build an updraught kiln considering safety,
fire the pellet vases in the updraught kiln observing safety precautions,
display own and others’ work for peer feedback and reflection.
key_inquiry_questions: How can you overcome the challenges in modeling using pellet technique?
What factors are considered when choosing a location for an updraught kiln?

sub_strands.title: Sculpture
learning_outcomes: a) examine the concept of relief sculpture for inspiration,
b) carve a relief sculpture for skill acquisation,
c) value own and others’ relief sculptural forms.
learning_experiences: explore virtual and/or actual samples of indigenous relief sculptures in Eastern and central Africa (Makonde, Akamba, Karamajong’ and Bamileke of DRC) emphasis on; subject matter, material, tools and finishing techniques,

design and carve a relief sculpture inspired by indigenous sculptures from East Africa, with emphasis on; - interpretation of subject matter - selection and preparation of appropriate recyclable material from the environment. - elements and principles of 3 D Art, - finishing
communicate with clarity as they display and critique own and others artwork.
key_inquiry_questions: How are the principles of 3D art portrayed in sculpture?
How can you experiment with organic and inorganic materials for a quality finish on relief sculptures?
